items.title: Ike Robertson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: I played with another band up there. We used to call him Kid Nicholas. We called him Wooden Jones.

ctx.x: Anything else you'd like to tell about the bands you played with?
I played with another band up there. We used to call him Kid Nicholas. We called him Wooden Jones.

items.title: Ike Robertson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: I played with his band a pretty good while.

ctx.x: That guy was like a mule. That guy could take a brass band out on the street by himself. Powerful. Yes, he used to call him Wooden Joe, and he was Wooden Joe too. Yeah, he was powerful. I played with his band a pretty good while. That was a dance band there?

items.title: Ike Robertson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: I was playing with Joe Nicholas.

ctx.x: Yeah, they get out early in the morning.

That's right. 7 o'clock. Yeah. I was playing with Joe Nicholas. We played for a little club up there on the... I see which street that was. It was really all from the Jefferson Buggers hall. It's supposed to start at 7 o'clock. Well, this drummer Arthur Hogan, he must have got there five to ten minutes after. I'm telling you, them guys cut up. The fella said, one of them said, he was late last carnival.
Maybe he couldn't get on the streetcar either the first time, you know, with his drummer.
